title: useEffect basics
summary: useEffect runs code after React paints the UI, usually to synchronize with something outside rendering.
whenToUse: Use it for browser APIs, network requests, subscriptions, timers, document title updates, and other side effects.
do: Use effects to synchronize with external systems.
Return a cleanup function when the effect starts something that must be stopped.
dont: Do not use an effect for values that can be calculated during render.
Do not put user event logic in an effect when it belongs in an event handler.

codeSnippets.title: Synchronize the document title
codeSnippets.description: Update a browser API after a value changes.
codeSnippets.explanation: The component renders first, then the effect keeps the browser tab title in sync with the current title.

commonMistake: Using useEffect to copy props or state into another state variable instead of deriving the value during render.
interviewAnswer: useEffect lets a component synchronize with external systems after rendering, such as APIs, browser features, subscriptions, or timers.

courseReference.notes: The movie detail view uses effects to fetch details and synchronize the document title.

title: useEffect dependency array
summary: The dependency array tells React which values should cause an effect to run again.
whenToUse: Use it whenever an effect reads props, state, or functions from the component scope.
do: Include every reactive value the effect reads.
Keep dependencies small by moving unrelated logic out of the effect.
Treat missing dependencies as a bug unless you have a specific reason.
dont: Do not omit dependencies to silence re-renders.
Do not use an empty array when the effect depends on changing props or state.

codeSnippets.title: Run when query changes
codeSnippets.description: A fetch effect should react to the value it uses.
codeSnippets.explanation: The effect runs after the first render and again whenever query changes.

codeSnippets.title: Run once on mount
codeSnippets.description: An empty dependency array is for effects that do not read changing component values.
codeSnippets.explanation: Because the effect reads no reactive values, it can run only after the component mounts.

commonMistake: Leaving a changing value out of the dependency array, which can make the effect use stale data.
interviewQuestion: What does the dependency array in useEffect do?
interviewAnswer: It tells React when to re-run the effect based on the reactive values the effect depends on.

courseReference.notes: The search effect depends on the current query, and the detail fetch depends on the selected movie id.

title: Fetching data with useEffect
summary: Fetch data in an effect when the request is caused by rendering a component with a specific state or prop.
whenToUse: Use it for simple client-side requests that should run when a search term, id, or filter changes.
do: Define an async function inside the effect and call it.
Track loading and error state around the request.
Guard against invalid inputs before starting the request.
dont: Do not make the effect callback itself async.
Do not ignore failed HTTP responses or API-level errors.

codeSnippets.title: Fetch results for a search query
codeSnippets.description: A small request flow with loading and error state.
codeSnippets.explanation: The effect reacts to query changes, clears old errors, shows loading, and stores either results or an error message.

commonMistake: Starting a request for every small invalid input change instead of guarding until the input is useful.
interviewQuestion: How do you fetch data in a React component with useEffect?
interviewAnswer: Create an async function inside the effect, call it, update loading/error/data state, and include the values that trigger the request in the dependency array.

courseReference.notes: The app fetches movie search results from an API when the query changes.

title: useEffect cleanup function
summary: An effect cleanup function runs before the effect runs again and when the component unmounts.
whenToUse: Use cleanup for event listeners, timers, subscriptions, in-flight requests, and temporary browser changes.
do: Remove event listeners that the effect adds.
Cancel or ignore stale async work when dependencies change.
Undo browser changes like document title when needed.
dont: Do not add a subscription without returning a cleanup.
Do not let older requests update state after newer requests have started.

codeSnippets.title: Clean up an event listener
codeSnippets.description: Remove the listener when the component unmounts or dependencies change.
codeSnippets.explanation: The cleanup prevents duplicate listeners and keeps the handler tied to the current onClose function.

codeSnippets.title: Abort a stale request
codeSnippets.description: Cancel an in-flight request when the search value changes.
codeSnippets.explanation: When query changes, React runs the cleanup first, aborting the old request before starting the next one.

commonMistake: Adding event listeners inside an effect but never removing them.
interviewQuestion: When does an effect cleanup function run?
interviewAnswer: It runs before the effect runs again because dependencies changed and when the component unmounts.

courseReference.notes: The app cleans up keyboard listeners, document title changes, and stale movie search requests.
